Linearizability notions in equivariant birational geometry

Andrew Kresch Address:  Institut für Mathematik, Universität Zürich, Winterthurerstrasse 190, CH-8057 Zürich, Switzerland Email address: andrew.kresch@math.uzh.ch and Yuri Tschinkel Address: Courant Institute

Date: June 8, 2026
Abstract.

We discuss birational properties of actions of finite groups on algebraic varieties, linearizability, torsors, and versality.

1. Introduction

In this note, we continue our study of equivariant birational geometry of regular actions of finite groups on smooth projective varieties over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. We amplify and expand the parallels between equivariant geometry and geometry over nonclosed fields, extending constructions from [DR15] to the setting of equivariant Chow groups, and equivariant decomposition of the diagonal. One of the key observations in [DR15] was that the twisting construction preserves some birational properties of GG-actions, e.g., a GG-variety is equivariantly stably linearizable if and only if all of its twists are stably rational.

Among our main results are:

  • •

    In Theorem 2.5 we show that many properties of arbitrary twists of GG-varieties via torsors (such as existence of rational points, unirationality, stable rationality, rationality) are implied by the same properties for a single twist, arising from a GG-variety with generically free versal GG-action.

  • •

    In Theorem 2.6 we show that birationality of twists of GG-varieties for all torsors is equivalent to birationality of twists arising from a single generically free versal GG-action.

  • •

    In Theorem 4.4 we prove that GG-equivariant integral decomposition of the diagonal, introduced in Section 4, is equivalent to integral decomposition of the diagonal for a twist arising from a single generically free versal actions.

Earlier developments have exhibited properties of arbitrary twists as implied by the same for a single twist, associated with a faithful GG-representation. As linearizable actions are versal, but not all versal actions are linearizable, for these properties our statements represent a strengthening.

In Section 2 we discuss basic notions in GG-equivariant birational geometry and their relation to birational geometry over nonclosed fields, via the twisting construction through torsors. In Section 3 we introduce the notions of coarse GG-birationality, which sits between GG-birationality and stable GG-birationality, and coarse linearizability. In Section 4 we define the notion of GG-equivariant decomposition of the diagonal and establish its key properties, e.g., connection with stable equivariant linearizability, in Theorem 4.6, and specialization, in Theorem 4.7. Finally, in Section 5, we consider the behavior of cohomological obstructions under twisting, and the related notion of negligible cohomology.

Acknowledgments: The authors thank Brendan Hassett and Sho Tanimoto for discussions and collaboration on related problems. The second author was partially supported by NSF grant 2301983.

2. Basic notions of equivariant birational geometry

We work over an algebraically closed field kk of characteristic zero.

Varieties over extension fields

For an extension field KK of kk, a variety over KK is a scheme of finite type over KK that is separated, reduced and irreducible. A proper birational map X⇢YX\dashrightarrow Y of varieties over KK is one that can be factored into proper birational morphisms and their formal inverses. Existence of a proper birational map over KK defines an equivalence relation, for which we employ the notation

X∼Y.X\sim Y.

For the stable version, with XX replaced by X×ℙmX\times{\mathbb{P}}^{m} and YY by Y×ℙnY\times{\mathbb{P}}^{n}, for some mm and nn, we employ the notation

X∼sY.X\sim^{s}Y.

We recall well-studied conditions for a variety XX over KK of dimension dd (understood for general XX as applied to a proper model of XX):

  • •

    rationality: X∼ℙdX\sim{\mathbb{P}}^{d},

  • •

    stable rationality: X∼sℙdX\sim^{s}{\mathbb{P}}^{d}.

GG-varieties

Let GG be a finite group. A GG-variety (over kk) is a separated, reduced, finite-type kk-scheme XX with regular GG-action, such that the GG-action is transitive on the set of irreducible components of XX. We call XX an irreducible GG-variety if, non-equivariantly, XX is irreducible, i.e., a variety. Given a GG-variety XX, the GG-action is generically free if it is free on an invariant dense open subvariety of XX. By convention, the actions are right GG-actions.

We recall some further notions; see, e.g., [KT26, §3.1] for more details. A GG-rational map is a GG-equivariant rational map between GG-varieties. A GG-birational map is a GG-rational map that is birational. A proper GG-birational map is one that factors as a composition of proper birational GG-equivariant morphisms and their formal inverses.

Among GG-varieties we have the relation, to be GG-birational:

X∼GY⇔∃ proper G-birational map X⇢Y.X\sim_{G}Y\quad\Leftrightarrow\quad\exists\text{ proper $G$-birational map $X\dashrightarrow Y$}.

We call XX and YY stably GG-birational if they become GG-birational after passing to products with (nonempty) projectivized representations:

X∼GsY⇔∃ G-representations U, V:X×ℙ(U)∼GY×ℙ(V).X\sim_{G}^{s}Y\quad\Leftrightarrow\quad\exists\text{ $G$-representations $U$, $V$}\colon X\times{\mathbb{P}}(U)\sim_{G}Y\times{\mathbb{P}}(V).

We also recall birationally invariant conditions on a GG-variety XX:

  • •

    (L) linearizability: X∼Gℙ(V)X\sim_{G}{\mathbb{P}}(V) for some representation VV.

  • •

    (SL) stable linearizability X×ℙ(U)∼Gℙ(V)X\times{\mathbb{P}}(U)\sim_{G}{\mathbb{P}}(V) for some representations UU and VV.

  • •

    (U) GG-unirationality if there is a dominant GG-rational map ℙ⁡(V)⇢X{\mathbb{P}}(V)\dashrightarrow X for some representation VV.

(These conditions apply as stated when XX is proper and are understood by convention for more general XX when they are satisfied by an equivariant proper model; cf. [KT26, §3.1].)

Torsors

Further notions are defined in terms of torsors, by which we mean torsors under GG. Without further mention, the base of the torsor will be Spec⁡(K)\mathrm{Spec}(K), where KK is an extension field of kk. The total space will be T=Spec⁡(L)T=\mathrm{Spec}(L) for an étale KK-algebra LL. The next condition on a GG-variety XX is defined by requiring a condition to hold for all torsors, over all extension fields KK of kk (expressed simply as ∀T:…\forall\,T\colon\dots).

  • •

    (WV) XX is weakly versal if ∀T\forall\,T: ∃\exists GG-equivariant Spec⁡(L)→X\mathrm{Spec}(L)\to X.

  • •

    (V) XX is versal if every invariant dense open subvariety of XX is weakly versal.

Let ZZ be a quasi-projective GG-variety over kk with a generically free action of GG and Z→Z/GZ\to Z/G the quotient. The function field k⁡(Z/G)k(Z/G) is the field of GG-invariants k​(Z)Gk(Z)^{G}. We get an associated torsor

TZ:=k⁡(Z)/k​(Z)G,T_{Z}:=k(Z)/k(Z)^{G},

corresponding to the Galois field extension, with Galois group GG. An important special case TVT_{V} arises from a faithful GG-representation VV and the quotient V→V/GV\to V/G.

Twisting

Given a torsor T=Spec⁡(L)T=\mathrm{Spec}(L) over KK, we obtain a free GG-action on the GG-variety

XL=X×Spec⁡(k)Spec⁡(L)X_{L}=X\times_{\mathrm{Spec}(k)}\mathrm{Spec}(L)

over KK. The quotient variety for this free GG-action, provided it exists, is the twist XT{}^{T}X, a variety over KK with the property (XT)L≅XL({}^{T}X)_{L}\cong X_{L}. The quotient variety is guaranteed to exist when XX is quasi-projective. In the sequel we will apply the twisting construction only to quasi-projective varieties.

When applied to a torsor TZT_{Z} arising from a generically free GG-action on ZZ as above, we get the twist XTZ{}^{T_{Z}}X over K=k​(Z)GK=k(Z)^{G}.

Example 2.1.

For a GG-representation VV of dimension n≥1n\geq 1, we have VT≅𝔸n{}^{T}V\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{n} [DR15, Lemma 3.1] and ℙT​(V)≅ℙn−1{}^{T}{\mathbb{P}}(V)\cong{\mathbb{P}}^{n-1}, for all torsors TT.

Remark 2.2.

The twisting construction respects GG-invariant loci U⊂XU\subset X, i.e., UT⊂XT{}^{T}U\subset{}^{T}X, for all GG-torsors TT. In particular, it preserves the stabilizer stratification on XX, see [KT26, Sect. 6.1].

Versality and twisting

Duncan and Reichstein give the following characterizations.

Proposition 2.3 ([DR15]).

Let XX be a quasi-projective GG-variety.

  • (i)

    XX is weakly versal ⇔∀T:XT​(K)≠∅\Leftrightarrow\,\forall\,T\colon{}^{T}X(K)\neq\emptyset.

  • (ii)

    XX is versal ⇔∀T:XT​(K)\Leftrightarrow\,\forall\,T\colon{}^{T}X(K) is dense in XT{}^{T}X.

  • (iii)

    XX is GG-unirational ⇔∀T:XT\Leftrightarrow\,\forall\,T\colon{}^{T}X is unirational.

  • (iv)

    XX is stably linearizable ⇔∀T:XT\Leftrightarrow\,\forall\,T\colon{}^{T}X is stably rational.

For smooth projective GG-varieties, these conditions are stably birationally invariant. Generally, we have the implications [DR15, (1.1)]:

(SL)⇒(U)⇒(V)⇒(WV).\textbf{(SL)}\quad\Rightarrow\quad\textbf{(U)}\quad\Rightarrow\quad\textbf{(V)}\quad\Rightarrow\quad\textbf{(WV)}.

(In [DR15], group actions satisfying (U) are called very versal.) There is also the implication

(WV)⇒(A)\textbf{(WV)}\quad\Rightarrow\quad\textbf{(A)}

[DR15, Rmk. 2.7], where Condition (A) is the existence of fixed points for all abelian subgroups of GG.

Example 2.4.

All of these implications are strict. For the first two, we see this already when GG is trivial [DR15, Sect. 1]. For G=ℤ/2​ℤG={\mathbb{Z}}/2{\mathbb{Z}}, the action on an elliptic curve EE by −1-1 has fixed points, thus is weakly versal [DR15, Prop. 2.2], but is not versal: for T:k⁡(t)/k⁡(t2)T\colon k(t)/k(t^{2}), the only rational points on the twist ET{}^{T}E are the ones coming from the fixed points. Actions satisfying condition (A), but not (WV), may be found among toric varieties and del Pezzo surfaces [KT25], [STZ26].

In the proof of their characterizations by means of torsors, Duncan and Reichstein make the observation that a property for all torsors is implied by the property for a single torsor, coming from a faithful GG-representation. Such observations had also appeared earlier, e.g., as recalled in [GM22, Prop. 2.1]. Our next result presents this observation uniformly for all of the relevant properties and in the strengthened form, that the single torsor can be given by any generically free versal group action.

Theorem 2.5.

Let XX be a quasi-projective GG-variety over kk, and 𝐏\mathbf{P} one of the following properties of a variety over an extension field of kk:

  • •

    possession of a rational point,

  • •

    possession of a Zariski dense set of rational points,

  • •

    unirationality,

  • •

    stable rationality,

  • •

    rationality.

The following are equivalent.

  • (i)

    For every torsor TT, the twist XT{}^{T}X satisfies property 𝐏\mathbf{P}.

  • (ii)

    For some quasi-projective GG-variety ZZ over kk with generically free versal GG-action and TZ=k⁡(Z)/k​(Z)GT_{Z}=k(Z)/k(Z)^{G}, the twist XTZ{}^{T_{Z}}X satisfies property 𝐏\mathbf{P}.

Proof.

The implication (i) ⇒\Rightarrow (ii) is trivial. We suppose (ii), and let KK be an extension field of kk and T:L/KT\colon L/K a GG-torsor, where LL is an étale KK-algebra. We need to establish property 𝐏\mathbf{P} for the twist XT{}^{T}X. We first treat the case when 𝐏\mathbf{P} is “possession of a rational point”, then we explain the modifications to the argument for the other properties 𝐏\mathbf{P}. If XTZ{}^{T_{Z}}X has a rational point, then there is a GG-rational map Z⇢XZ\dashrightarrow X, say, defined on invariant dense open U⊂ZU\subset Z. Since the GG-action on ZZ is versal, there is a GG-equivariant morphism Spec⁡(L)→U\mathrm{Spec}(L)\to U. Composing, we get equivariant Spec⁡(L)→X\mathrm{Spec}(L)\to X, thus a KK-point of XT{}^{T}X.

Generally, density of a given set of points of a finite-type scheme over a field is stable under field extension (reduce to the case of a finitely generated field extension and treat the finite and purely transcendental cases separately). So, if XTZ{}^{T_{Z}}X has a dense set of k​(Z)Gk(Z)^{G}-points, then XK⁡(Z)/K​(Z)G{}^{K(Z)/K(Z)^{G}}X has a dense set of K​(Z)GK(Z)^{G}-points. For invariant dense open W⊂XKW\subset X_{K} we argue as above with ZK⇢WZ_{K}\dashrightarrow W, defined on invariant dense open U⊂ZKU\subset Z_{K}, and get a KK-point of XT{}^{T}X, for which the corresponding GG-equivariant morphism Spec⁡(L)→XK\mathrm{Spec}(L)\to X_{K} has image in WW.

If XTZ{}^{T_{Z}}X is unirational, then for some NN there exists a dominant GG-rational map ℙN×Z⇢X×Z{\mathbb{P}}^{N}\times Z\dashrightarrow X\times Z (with trivial action on ℙN{\mathbb{P}}^{N}), compatible with the projection morphisms to ZZ. We choose an invariant dense open subset where this is a morphism and an invariant dense open subset WW of the image and let U⊂ZU\subset Z denote the image of W⊂X×ZW\subset X\times Z under projection. As before, by versality, there is equivariant Spec⁡(L)→U\mathrm{Spec}(L)\to U, and by base change, dominant equivariant ℙLN⇢XL{\mathbb{P}}^{N}_{L}\dashrightarrow X_{L}, hence dominant ℙKN⇢XT{\mathbb{P}}^{N}_{K}\dashrightarrow{}^{T}X.

For the remaining properties, we get the result as a special case of the next theorem. ∎

Theorem 2.6.

Let XX and YY be a quasi-projective GG-varieties over kk. The following are equivalent.

  • (i)

    For every torsor TT, we have XT∼YT{}^{T}X\sim{}^{T}Y.

  • (ii)

    For some quasi-projective GG-variety ZZ over kk with generically free versal GG-action, we have XTZ∼YTZ{}^{T_{Z}}X\sim{}^{T_{Z}}Y.

Proof.

As before, (i) ⇒\Rightarrow (ii) is trivial, so we suppose (ii) and consider a GG-torsor T:L/KT\colon L/K. By a closure-of-graph construction we have, after replacing ZZ by a suitable invariant dense open subvariety, a diagram of equivariant projective birational morphisms

compatible with projection morphisms to ZZ. We let W⊂VW\subset V be an invariant dense open subset, such that the morphisms in the diagram restrict to isomorphisms of VV with the respective images. Let U⊂ZU\subset Z to be the common image under the further projection morphisms. We conclude as in the proof of Theorem 2.5 with an equivariant morphism Spec⁡(L)→U\mathrm{Spec}(L)\to U and base change. ∎

3. Coarse GG-birationality and coarse linearizability

Theorem 2.6 motivates the following definition.

Definition 3.1.

Two quasi-projective GG-varieties XX and YY are said to be coarsely GG-birational, written

X∼GcYX\sim_{G}^{c}Y

if the equivalent conditions of Theorem 2.6 hold for XX and YY.

Example 3.2.

We have ℙ(V)∼Gcℙn−1{\mathbb{P}}(V)\sim_{G}^{c}{\mathbb{P}}^{n-1} for any GG-representation VV of dimension n≥1n\geq 1 (cf. Example 2.1).

We recall that the case Y=ℙdY={\mathbb{P}}^{d} of Theorem 2.6, where dd denotes the dimension of XX, gives Theorem 2.5 for the property rationality.

Definition 3.3.

We say that a projective GG-variety XX is coarsely linearizable, or satisfies Condition (CL), if XX satisfies the equivalent conditions of Theorem 2.5 for the property rationality. Generally, a GG-variety considered to satisfy Condition (CL), when (CL) holds for an equivariant projective model.

In other words, for a projective GG-variety XX of dimension dd:

X is coarsely linearizable⇔X∼Gcℙd.\text{$X$ is coarsely linearizable}\quad\Leftrightarrow\quad X\sim_{G}^{c}{\mathbb{P}}^{d}.
Example 3.4.

The obstruction to linearizability, based on dimension of GG-representations [KT26, §4.1], yields examples of actions that are coarsely linearizable but not linearizable. Letting the symmetric group 𝔖3\mathfrak{S}_{3} act faithfully on ℙ1{\mathbb{P}}^{1}, the product action of 𝔖3×𝔖3\mathfrak{S}_{3}\times\mathfrak{S}_{3} on ℙ1×ℙ1{\mathbb{P}}^{1}\times{\mathbb{P}}^{1} is coarsely linearizable but not linearizable: the smallest faithful representation of 𝔖3×𝔖3\mathfrak{S}_{3}\times\mathfrak{S}_{3} has dimension 44. For additional examples, notice that (CL) ⇔\Leftrightarrow (SL) for any nonsingular invariant quadric X⊂ℙ⁡(V)X\subset{\mathbb{P}}(V). So a stably linearizable dimension-obstructed quadric, as given in [KT26, §4.1], is coarsely linearizable but not linearizable.

Example 3.5.

Some varieties are known to have the property that all twists are rational, or at least all twists with a rational point are rational. Examples include projective spaces, quadric hypersurfaces, del Pezzo surfaces of degree ≥5\geq 5, and quintic del Pezzo threefolds and prime Fano threefolds of genus 7 and 12 [KP23, Thm. 1.1]. On the other hand, methods such as universal torsors or vector bundle techniques give the stable linearizability of some nonlinearizable actions. Combining, we get additional examples of actions that are coarsely linearizable but not linearizable. These include a sextic del Pezzo surface with 𝔖4\mathfrak{S}_{4}-action [HT23, Sect. 5.2], ℳ¯0,2​n+1\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,2n+1} for many subgroups of 𝔖2​n+1\mathfrak{S}_{2n+1} [HTZ25], and some actions on quadrics [BGvBT25, Prop. 12].

Remark 3.6.

Condition (CL) fits into a chain of implications

(L)⇒(CL)⇒(SL).\textbf{(L)}\quad\Rightarrow\quad\textbf{(CL)}\quad\Rightarrow\quad\textbf{(SL)}.

As we see in Examples 3.4 and 3.5, the first implication cannot be reversed. When GG is the trivial group, (L) and (CL) are both equivalent to rationality, and (SL), to stable rationality. Since there are known examples of stably rational varieties that are not rational [BCTSSD85], also the second implication cannot be reversed.

Example 3.7.

We let the quaternion group 𝔔8\mathfrak{Q}_{8} act linearly on ℙ1{\mathbb{P}}^{1}, via faithful action of the 𝔎4\mathfrak{K}_{4}-quotient, with center Z⊂𝔔8Z\subset\mathfrak{Q}_{8} acting trivially. The product action of G=𝔔8×𝔔8G=\mathfrak{Q}_{8}\times\mathfrak{Q}_{8} on X=ℙ1×ℙ1X={\mathbb{P}}^{1}\times{\mathbb{P}}^{1} has trivial action of Z×ZZ\times Z. Since any ℙ⁡(V){\mathbb{P}}(V), dim(V)=3\dim(V)=3, has trivial action of a subgroup of GG of order ≥8\geq 8, the action is not linearizable. Being a product of linear actions, it is coarsely linearizable. Thus it is also stably linearizable. It is also interesting to note that X×ℙnX\times{\mathbb{P}}^{n} is not linearizable for any nn, where GG acts trivially on the factor ℙn{\mathbb{P}}^{n}. Indeed, if X×ℙn∼Gℙ(V)X\times{\mathbb{P}}^{n}\sim_{G}{\mathbb{P}}(V), then Z×ZZ\times Z must act trivially on ℙ⁡(V){\mathbb{P}}(V), thus X×ℙn∼𝔎4×𝔎4ℙ(V)X\times{\mathbb{P}}^{n}\sim_{\mathfrak{K}_{4}\times\mathfrak{K}_{4}}{\mathbb{P}}(V). This would contradict the equivariant birational invariance of the Amitsur group Am2\mathrm{Am}^{2}; cf. [KT26, Sect. 5]:

Am2​(X×ℙn,𝔎4×𝔎4)≅ℤ/2​ℤ⊕ℤ/2​ℤ,\mathrm{Am}^{2}(X\times{\mathbb{P}}^{n},\mathfrak{K}_{4}\times\mathfrak{K}_{4})\cong{\mathbb{Z}}/2{\mathbb{Z}}\oplus{\mathbb{Z}}/2{\mathbb{Z}},

but any projective space has cyclic Am2\mathrm{Am}^{2}.

Remark 3.8.

Example 3.7 illustrates why (SL) needs to be defined by the condition X×ℙ(U)∼Gℙ(V)X\times{\mathbb{P}}(U)\sim_{G}{\mathbb{P}}(V), rather than the linearizability of X×ℙnX\times{\mathbb{P}}^{n} for some nn. For generically free actions, the two formulations are equivalent, since then we have X×ℙ(U)∼GX×ℙnX\times{\mathbb{P}}(U)\sim_{G}X\times{\mathbb{P}}^{n}, n=dim(U)−1n=\dim(U)-1, by the No-Name Lemma; cf. [KT26, §3.5].

Proposition 3.9.

For projective GG-varieties XX and YY we have:

X∼GY⇒X∼GcY⇒X∼GsY.X\sim_{G}Y\quad\Rightarrow\quad X\sim_{G}^{c}Y\quad\Rightarrow\quad X\sim_{G}^{s}Y.
Proof.

The first implication is clear. For the second, we take VV to be a GG-representation, such that the GG-action on ℙ⁡(V){\mathbb{P}}(V) is generically free, and apply Theorem 2.6 to the versal GG-action on Z=ℙ⁡(V)Z={\mathbb{P}}(V). A birational equivalence XTZ∼YTZ{}^{T_{Z}}X\sim{}^{T_{Z}}Y gives an equivariant birational equivalence X×ℙ(V)∼GY×ℙ(V)X\times{\mathbb{P}}(V)\sim_{G}Y\times{\mathbb{P}}(V). ∎

Remark 3.10.

Condition (SL) may be formulated equivalently with (compactifications of) representations, rather than projectivized representations, as is done, for instance, in [DR15, Sect. 1]. We summarize other reformulations here. Let UU and VV be GG-representations of respective dimensions dd, e≥1e\geq 1, and WW a GG-representation, such that the GG-action on ℙ⁡(W){\mathbb{P}}(W) is generically free. Suppose that

X×ℙ(U)∼GY×ℙ(V).X\times{\mathbb{P}}(U)\sim_{G}Y\times{\mathbb{P}}(V).

Then the same holds after passing to products with ℙ⁡(W){\mathbb{P}}(W). The No-Name Lemma gives

ℙ(U)×ℙ(W)∼Gℙ(1d⊕W) and ℙ(V)×ℙ(W)∼Gℙ(1e⊕W);{\mathbb{P}}(U)\times{\mathbb{P}}(W)\sim_{G}{\mathbb{P}}(1^{d}\oplus W)\quad\text{ and }\quad{\mathbb{P}}(V)\times{\mathbb{P}}(W)\sim_{G}{\mathbb{P}}(1^{e}\oplus W);

cf. [KT26, Cor. 3.3]). So

X×ℙ(1d⊕W)∼GY×ℙ(1e⊕W).X\times{\mathbb{P}}(1^{d}\oplus W)\sim_{G}Y\times{\mathbb{P}}(1^{e}\oplus W).

In particular, XX is stably linearizable if and only if

X×ℙ(1d⊕W)∼Gℙ(1e⊕W),X\times{\mathbb{P}}(1^{d}\oplus W)\sim_{G}{\mathbb{P}}(1^{e}\oplus W),

for some dd, e≥1e\geq 1. Also, if XX and YY have the same dimension, then there is no loss of generality in taking U=VU=V in the definition of X∼GsYX\sim_{G}^{s}Y.

Example 3.11.

Taking YY to be ℙ⁡(V){\mathbb{P}}(V) in Proposition 3.9 recovers the chain of implications among the notions of linearizability. By definition, (L) is the condition X∼Gℙ(V)X\sim_{G}{\mathbb{P}}(V) for some VV. By Example 3.2, (CL) is equivalent to the condition X∼Gcℙ(V)X\sim_{G}^{c}{\mathbb{P}}(V) for some VV. Arguing as in Remark 3.10, (SL) is equivalent to X∼Gsℙ(V)X\sim_{G}^{s}{\mathbb{P}}(V) for some VV.

Conditions (U), (SL), and (L) are defined via GG-equivariant geometry, while (WV), (V), and the new Condition (CL) are defined in terms of torsors. We now give interpretations in terms of equivariant geometry.

Proposition 3.12.

Let XX be a GG-variety. Let WW be a GG-representation, such that GG acts generically freely on ℙ⁡(W){\mathbb{P}}(W). The following are equivalent.

  • (i)

    The GG-action on XX is weakly versal.

  • (ii)

    For some GG-representation VV of positive dimension, there is a GG-rational map ℙ⁡(V)⇢X{\mathbb{P}}(V)\dashrightarrow X.

  • (iii)

    There is a GG-rational map ℙ⁡(W)⇢X{\mathbb{P}}(W)\dashrightarrow X.

Proof.

In the proof we use the following form of Theorem 2.5, which makes no reference to twists:

(WV)⇔∃ G-rational Z⇢X\text{{(WV)}}\quad\Leftrightarrow\quad\exists\text{ $G$-rational }Z\dashrightarrow X

(where ZZ is as in Theorem 2.5). The implication (iii) ⇒\Rightarrow (ii) is trivial. Given (ii), there is also a GG-rational map ℙ⁡(V)×ℙ⁡(W)⇢X{\mathbb{P}}(V)\times{\mathbb{P}}(W)\dashrightarrow X; so we obain Condition (WV) by taking Z=ℙ⁡(V)×ℙ⁡(W)Z={\mathbb{P}}(V)\times{\mathbb{P}}(W). Taking Z=ℙ⁡(W)Z={\mathbb{P}}(W), we get (i) ⇒\Rightarrow (iii). ∎

The next statement makes reference to the image closure of a rational map, which is the closure of the image of any dense open on which the map is defined.

Proposition 3.13.

Let XX be a GG-variety. Let WW be a GG-representation, such that GG acts generically freely on ℙ⁡(W){\mathbb{P}}(W). The following are equivalent.

  • (i)

    The GG-action on XX is versal.

  • (ii)

    The union of image closures of GG-rational maps ℙ⁡(V)⇢X{\mathbb{P}}(V)\dashrightarrow X, over all GG-representations VV, is dense in XX.

  • (iii)

    The union of image closures of GG-rational maps ℙ⁡(W)⇢X{\mathbb{P}}(W)\dashrightarrow X is dense in XX.

Proof.

This is immediate from Proposition 3.12. ∎

Proposition 3.14.

Let XX and YY be quasi-projective GG-varieties. Let WW be a GG-representation, such that GG acts generically freely on ℙ⁡(W){\mathbb{P}}(W). Then XX and YY are coarsely GG-birational, if and only if there exists a proper GG-birational map X×ℙ⁡(W)⇢Y×ℙ⁡(W)X\times{\mathbb{P}}(W)\dashrightarrow Y\times{\mathbb{P}}(W), fitting in a commutative diagram

with the projection morphisms to ℙ⁡(W){\mathbb{P}}(W).

Proof.

We apply Theorem 2.6 and use that a proper birational map of twists XTZ∼YTZ{}^{T_{Z}}X\sim{}^{T_{Z}}Y comes from a proper GG-birational map of products with ZZ, compatible with the projection maps to ZZ. ∎

Corollary 3.15.

Let XX be a projective GG-variety of dimension dd. Let WW be a GG-representation, such that GG acts generically freely on ℙ⁡(W){\mathbb{P}}(W). The following are equivalent.

  • (i)

    The GG-action on XX is coarsely linearizable.

  • (ii)

    There exists a GG-birational map X×ℙ⁡(W)⇢ℙd×ℙ⁡(W)X\times{\mathbb{P}}(W)\dashrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}^{d}\times{\mathbb{P}}(W), that is compatible with the projection morphisms to ℙ⁡(W){\mathbb{P}}(W).

Remark 3.16.

The implications, among the conditions on smooth projective GG-varieties mentioned so far, are displayed here in one chain:

(L)⇒(CL)⇒(SL)⇒(U)⇒(V)⇒(WV)⇒(A).\textbf{(L)}\ \Rightarrow\ \textbf{(CL)}\ \Rightarrow\ \textbf{(SL)}\ \Rightarrow\ \textbf{(U)}\ \Rightarrow\ \textbf{(V)}\ \Rightarrow\ \textbf{(WV)}\ \Rightarrow\ \textbf{(A)}.

The strictness of these implications is explained, for the first two implications, in Remark 3.6, and for the remaining ones, in Example 2.4.

4. Decomposition of the diagonal

Equivariant Chow groups

Let XX be a quasi-projective GG-variety over kk, of dimension nn. We recall the definition of equivariant Chow groups

CHiG​(X):=CHi+ℓ​((X×U)/G),\mathrm{CH}_{i}^{G}(X):=\mathrm{CH}_{i+\ell}((X\times U)/G),

with diagonal action of GG on XX and on UU, a GG-invariant Zariski open subset of an ℓ\ell-dimensional GG-representation VV, such that GG acts freely on UU and codim⁡(V∖U)>n−i\mathrm{codim}(V\setminus U)>n-i; see [EG98]. This does not depend on VV and UU.

An ii-dimensional GG-invariant cycle on XX, as well as an (i+ℓ)(i+\ell)-dimensional GG-invariant cycle on X×VX\times V, define classes in CHiG​(X)\mathrm{CH}_{i}^{G}(X). Taking XX to be a point yields

CHiG:=CHiG​(Spec⁡(k)),\mathrm{CH}^{G}_{i}:=\mathrm{CH}^{G}_{i}(\mathrm{Spec}(k)),

the case treated in [Tot99]. Analogous to the degree map of a proper variety, when XX is projective we have

degiG:CHiG​(X)→CHiG.\deg_{i}^{G}\colon\mathrm{CH}_{i}^{G}(X)\to\mathrm{CH}_{i}^{G}.

For i=0i=0 we have CHiG=ℤ\mathrm{CH}_{i}^{G}={\mathbb{Z}} and thus integer-valued deg0G\deg_{0}^{G}, as in the non-equivariant case.

Lemma 4.1.

[EG98, Proposition 1] If α∈CHiG​(X)\alpha\in\mathrm{CH}^{G}_{i}(X), then there exists an ℓ\ell-dimensional GG-representation VV, and an (i+ℓ)(i+\ell)-dimensional GG-invariant cycle Z=∑ai​[Zi]Z=\sum a_{i}[Z_{i}] on X×VX\times V, that represents the class of α\alpha.

Finally, over a kk-point of U/GU/G, the fiber of

(X×U)/G→U/G(X\times U)/G\to U/G

is isomorphic to XX. Pullback to a fiber gives a homomorphism

CHiG​(X)→CHi​(X),\mathrm{CH}_{i}^{G}(X)\to\mathrm{CH}_{i}(X),

which is independent of the choice of fiber. The image is contained in the GG-invariant subgroup CHi​(X)G\mathrm{CH}_{i}(X)^{G}.

Equivariant decomposition of the diagonal

Let XX be a projective variety of dimension nn over a field KK. We recall, XX is said to have integral decomposition of the diagonal if there exist a zero-dimensional cycle class ζ∈CH0​(X)\zeta\in\mathrm{CH}_{0}(X) of degree 11 and closed D⊊XD\subsetneq X, such that the class of the diagonal ΔX\Delta_{X} satisfies

[ΔX]=([X]×ζ)+γ[\Delta_{X}]=([X]\times\zeta)+\gamma

in CHn​(X×X)\mathrm{CH}_{n}(X\times X), for an nn-dimensional cycle class γ\gamma, supported on D×XD\times X. This implies that ζ=[x]\zeta=[x] in CH0​(X)\mathrm{CH}_{0}(X), for any smooth KK-point xx in the complement of DD (by restriction to x×Xx\times X). Thus, if X⁡(K)X(K) is dense in XX, the definition may be equivalently stated with the existence of a smooth KK-point xx, taking the place of ζ\zeta in the equality.

Definition 4.2.

Let XX be an irreducible projective GG-variety of dimension nn. We say that XX has GG-equivariant integral decomposition of the diagonal if there exist ζ∈CH0G​(X)\zeta\in\mathrm{CH}_{0}^{G}(X), with deg0G⁡(ζ)=1\deg^{G}_{0}(\zeta)=1, and GG-invariant closed D⊊XD\subsetneq X, such that

(4.1) [ΔX]=([X]×ζ)+γ[\Delta_{X}]=([X]\times\zeta)+\gamma

in CHnG​(X×X)\mathrm{CH}_{n}^{G}(X\times X), for some γ∈im⁡(CHnG​(D×X)→CHnG​(X×X))\gamma\in\mathrm{im}(\mathrm{CH}^{G}_{n}(D\times X)\to\mathrm{CH}^{G}_{n}(X\times X)).

Lemma 4.3.

Let KK be a field, XX a finite-type KK-scheme, ℓ\ell a positive integer, and S⊊𝔸KℓS\subsetneq{\mathbb{A}}^{\ell}_{K} a closed subscheme. The inclusion map

X×S→X×𝔸KℓX\times S\to X\times{\mathbb{A}}^{\ell}_{K}

induces, by pushforward, the zero map on Chow groups.

Proof.

Pullback gives an isomorphism CHi​(X)→CHi+ℓ​(X×𝔸Kℓ)\mathrm{CH}_{i}(X)\to\mathrm{CH}_{i+\ell}(X\times{\mathbb{A}}^{\ell}_{K}), with inverse given by intersection with X×{v}X\times\{v\} for any KK-point v∈𝔸Kℓv\in{\mathbb{A}}^{\ell}_{K}. So it suffices to show the vanishing of the composite

CHi+ℓ​(X×S)→CHi+ℓ​(X×𝔸Kℓ)→CHi​(X)\mathrm{CH}_{i+\ell}(X\times S)\to\mathrm{CH}_{i+\ell}(X\times{\mathbb{A}}^{\ell}_{K})\to\mathrm{CH}_{i}(X)

with the inverse isomorphism. This is clear if KK is infinite, by choosing v∈𝔸Kℓ∖Sv\in{\mathbb{A}}^{\ell}_{K}\setminus S, while the case that KK is finite can be treated with a pair of points vv, v′v^{\prime} valued in extension fields of KK of coprime degrees. ∎

Theorem 4.4.

Let XX be an irreducible projective GG-variety over kk with generically free GG-action. The following are equivalent.

  • (i)

    For every torsor TT, XT{}^{T}X has integral decomposition of the diagonal.

  • (ii)

    For some quasi-projective GG-variety ZZ over kk with generically free versal GG-action, XTZ{}^{T_{Z}}X has integral decomposition of the diagonal.

  • (iii)

    XX has GG-equivariant integral decomposition of the diagonal.

Proof.

The implication (i) ⇒\Rightarrow (ii) is trivial. We show (ii) ⇒\Rightarrow (i). Let dd denote the dimension of ZZ. An integral decomposition of the diagonal determines, by spreading out, an expression in CHn+d​((X×X×Y)/G)\mathrm{CH}_{n+d}((X\times X\times Y)/G)

(4.2) [(ΔX×Y)/G]=∑iai​[(X×Yi)/G]+γ,[(\Delta_{X}\times Y)/G]=\sum_{i}a_{i}[(X\times Y_{i})/G]+\gamma,

for some dense invariant open Y⊂ZY\subset Z, without loss of generality contained in the nonsingular locus of ZZ, integers aia_{i}, invariant multisections Yi⊂X×YY_{i}\subset X\times Y, flat over YY, of the projection map X×Y→YX\times Y\to Y, of respective degrees did_{i}, with ∑ai​di=1\sum a_{i}d_{i}=1, and class γ\gamma of an invariant cycle supported on D×X×YD\times X\times Y, for some GG-invariant closed D⊊XD\subsetneq X. Given a torsor T:L/KT\colon L/K, we take GG-equivariant Spec⁡(L)→Y\mathrm{Spec}(L)\to Y, say dominant over GG-invariant closed Y′⊂YY^{\prime}\subset Y of codimension cc. The inclusion gives rise to a Gysin pullback, hence an analogous expression in CHn+d−c​((X×X×Y′)/G)\mathrm{CH}_{n+d-c}((X\times X\times Y^{\prime})/G). We restrict over the generic point of Y′/GY^{\prime}/G and extend scalars to obtain an integral decomposition of the diagonal on XT{}^{T}X.

Taking Z=VZ=V, a GG-representation of dimension ℓ\ell with GG-invariant open U⊂VU\subset V with free GG-action, codim⁡(V∖U)>n\mathrm{codim}(V\setminus U)>n, gives (iii) ⇒\Rightarrow (ii). We complete the proof by showing (i) ⇒\Rightarrow (iii). By (i), we have integral decomposition of the diagonal for the twist by torsor TVT_{V}, where we are taking Z=VZ=V. Spreading out, we may suppose that we have an expression (4.2). Let W=V∖YW=V\setminus Y. Taking closures, from (4.2) we get

[(ΔX×V)/G]=∑ai​[(X×Y¯i)/G]+γ+δ,[(\Delta_{X}\times V)/G]=\sum a_{i}[(X\times\overline{Y}_{i})/G]+\gamma+\delta,

with γ\gamma supported on D×X×VD\times X\times V and δ\delta supported on X×X×WX\times X\times W. Let T=TXT=T_{X}, the torsor L/KL/K with L=k⁡(X)L=k(X) and K=k​(X)GK=k(X)^{G}. With base change by Spec⁡(K)→X/G\mathrm{Spec}(K)\to X/G and an identification VTX≅𝔸Kℓ{}^{T_{X}}V\cong{\mathbb{A}}^{\ell}_{K}, yielding from WW closed S⊊𝔸KℓS\subsetneq{\mathbb{A}}^{\ell}_{K}, we obtain from δ\delta a cycle class, supported on XTX×S{}^{T_{X}}X\times S. By Lemma 4.3 this is rationally equivalent to 00 on XTX×𝔸Kℓ{}^{T_{X}}X\times{\mathbb{A}}^{\ell}_{K}. Spreading out, we obtain a rational equivalence on (X×X×V)/G(X\times X\times V)/G between δ\delta and γ′\gamma^{\prime} for a class γ′\gamma^{\prime} of an invariant cycle supported on D′×X×VD^{\prime}\times X\times V, for some invariant closed D′⊊XD^{\prime}\subsetneq X. Thus, XX satisfies GG-equivariant integral decomposition of the diagonal. ∎

Remark 4.5.

If the GG-action on XX is generically free and versal, then Definition 4.2 may be equivalently stated with ζ\zeta represented by an invariant U~⊂X×U\widetilde{U}\subset X\times U, projecting birationally to UU, with U~⊄Xsing×U\widetilde{U}\not\subset X^{\mathrm{sing}}\times U. Indeed, versality implies density of rational points on any twist XT{}^{T}X. In the portion of the proof with T=TVT=T_{V} and Z=VZ=V, over K=k​(V)GK=k(V)^{G} we use the observation that integral decomposition of the diagonal may be equivalently stated with a smooth KK-point in the role of ζ\zeta. We carry out the proof of (i) ⇒\Rightarrow (iii) in Theorem 4.4 with just a single index i=1i=1, an equivariant section Y1Y_{1}, and a1=1a_{1}=1, to get what is claimed, with U~=(X×U)∩Y¯1\widetilde{U}=(X\times U)\cap\overline{Y}_{1}.

As is well known (cf. [Sal84, Sect. 3] and [CTP16, Lemma 1.5]), stably rational varieties admit an integral decomposition of the diagonal. Here we give an analogous result in equivariant birational geometry.

Theorem 4.6.

Let GG be a finite group and XX a smooth projective variety with a generically free GG-action. If the action is stably linearizable then XX admits a GG-equivariant integral decomposition of the diagonal.

Proof.

Theorem 4.4 reduces the statement to stable rationality of twists of XX. ∎

The following is analogous to [Voi15, Thm. 2.1] and [CTP16, Thm. 2.3].

Theorem 4.7.

Let GG be a finite group. Let π:𝒳→B\pi:\mathcal{X}\to B be a smooth proper family of irreducible GG-varieties over a smooth curve BB such that GG acts on 𝒳\mathcal{X} and π\pi is GG-invariant. Suppose that the general fiber 𝒳b\mathcal{X}_{b} has a GG-equivariant integral decomposition of the diagonal. Then a special fiber 𝒳b0\mathcal{X}_{b_{0}} has a GG-equivariant integral decomposition of the diagonal.

Proof.

This follows from [CTP16, Thm. 1.12] combined with Theorem 4.4. ∎

5. Cohomological invariants

Cohomology, and in particular, the Leray spectral sequence associated to the morphism of stacks

[X/G]→B​G,[X/G]\to BG,

supplies equivariant birational invariants of GG-actions. In this section, we investigate the behavior of these under passage to nonclosed fields, via the twisting construction in Section 2.

Universal torsor obstruction and Amitsur invariants

We recall the definition of the Amitsur invariant

Am2​(X,G):=Pic​(X)G/Pic⁡([X/G])\mathrm{Am}^{2}(X,G):=\mathrm{Pic}(X)^{G}/\mathrm{Pic}([X/G])

in equivariant geometry; see, e.g., [BCDP23]. This group captures obstructions to the GG-linearization of GG-invariant classes in Pic⁡(X)\mathrm{Pic}(X). When XX is a smooth projective irreducible GG-variety, Am2​(X,G)\mathrm{Am}^{2}(X,G) can be expressed as the image of the homomorphism

δ2:Pic​(X)G→H2​(G,k×)\delta_{2}\colon\mathrm{Pic}(X)^{G}\to{\mathrm{H}}^{2}(G,k^{\times})

from the Leray spectral sequence. Higher Amitsur invariants Amd​(X,G)\mathrm{Am}^{d}(X,G) (d≥2d\geq 2) are defined similarly, as the images of homomorphisms

δd:Hd−2​(G,Pic⁡(X))→Hd​(G,k×).\delta_{d}\colon{\mathrm{H}}^{d-2}(G,\mathrm{Pic}(X))\to{\mathrm{H}}^{d}(G,k^{\times}).

Assume that Pic⁡(X)\mathrm{Pic}(X) is ℤ{\mathbb{Z}}-free and finitely generated. A similar spectral sequence gives rise to an exact sequence [KT25, (3.1)]

(5.1) HG1​(X,TNS)→End​(Pic⁡(X))G→∂H2​(G,TNS​(k))→HG2​(X,TNS),{\mathrm{H}}^{1}_{G}(X,T_{\mathrm{NS}})\to\mathrm{End}(\mathrm{Pic}(X))^{G}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\partial}}{{\to}}{\mathrm{H}}^{2}(G,T_{\mathrm{NS}}(k))\to{\mathrm{H}}^{2}_{G}(X,T_{\mathrm{NS}}),

where TNST_{\mathrm{NS}} denotes the Néron-Severi torus, and we have the universal torsor obstruction

β⁡(X​ý​G):=∂(1Pic⁡(X)).\beta(X\righttoleftarrow G):=\partial(1_{\mathrm{Pic}(X)}).

The Amitsur invariants Amd​(X,G)\mathrm{Am}^{d}(X,G) (d≥2d\geq 2) and the vanishing of the universal torsor obstruction β⁡(X​ý​G)\beta(X\righttoleftarrow G) are stable GG-birational invariants of XX. As well, β⁡(X​ý​G)=0\beta(X\righttoleftarrow G)=0 implies Amd​(X,G)=0\mathrm{Am}^{d}(X,G)=0 for all d≥2d\geq 2 [STZ26, Thm. 1.2].

Proposition 5.1.

Let XX be a smooth projective irreducible GG-variety, such that the GG-action is weakly versal. Then:

  • (i)

    Amd​(X,G)=0\mathrm{Am}^{d}(X,G)=0, for all d≥2d\geq 2.

  • (ii)

    If Pic⁡(X)\mathrm{Pic}(X) is ℤ{\mathbb{Z}}-free and finitely generated, then β⁡(X​ý​G)=0\beta(X\righttoleftarrow G)=0.

Proof.

Assertion (i) is immediate from [STZ26, Thm. 5.1]. Assertion (ii) is [KT25, Thm. 5.3], where the stated hypothesis that XX is rational can be replaced by the more general condition, that Pic⁡(X)\mathrm{Pic}(X) is ℤ{\mathbb{Z}}-free and finitely generated. ∎

Let XX be a variety over an extension field KK of kk. We denote by K¯\overline{K} an algebraic closure and by 𝔤K\mathfrak{g}_{K} the absolute Galois group of KK. Then there is a similar, classical, invariant

Am2​(X):=Pic​(XK¯)𝔤K/Pic⁡(X).\mathrm{Am}^{2}(X):=\mathrm{Pic}(X_{\overline{K}})^{\mathfrak{g}_{K}}/\mathrm{Pic}(X).

In case XX is a nonsingular geometrically irreducible projective variety over KK, we identify Am2​(X)\mathrm{Am}^{2}(X) with the subgroup of the Brauer group Br⁡(K)≃H2​(𝔤K,K¯×)\mathrm{Br}(K)\simeq{\mathrm{H}}^{2}(\mathfrak{g}_{K},\overline{K}^{\times}), that arises as the image of Pic​(XK¯)𝔤K\mathrm{Pic}(X_{\overline{K}})^{\mathfrak{g}_{K}} from the analogous spectral sequence.

Negligible cohomology

We recall the definition and basic properties, following [GM22]. A continuous homomorphism

ρK:𝔤K→G\rho_{K}\colon\mathfrak{g}_{K}\to G

yields a homomorphism in cohomology

ρK∗:Hd​(G,M)→Hd​(𝔤K,M),\rho_{K}^{*}\colon{\mathrm{H}}^{d}(G,M)\to{\mathrm{H}}^{d}(\mathfrak{g}_{K},M),

for every GG-module MM. The group of negligible classes

Hd(G,M)neg:={α∣ρK∗(α)=0,∀K/k}⊆Hd(G,M){\mathrm{H}}^{d}(G,M)_{\mathrm{neg}}:=\{\alpha\mid\rho_{K}^{*}(\alpha)=0,\quad\forall\,K/k\}\subseteq{\mathrm{H}}^{d}(G,M)

consists of classes not detectable in Galois cohomology. In particular, this applies to the twisting construction associated with a quasi-projective GG-variety ZZ with generically free GG-action, in which case there is a natural surjective homomorphism ρZ:𝔤k​(Z)G→G\rho_{Z}\colon\mathfrak{g}_{k(Z)^{G}}\to G, arising from the Galois extension k⁡(Z)/k​(Z)Gk(Z)/k(Z)^{G}.

The following result strengthens [GM22, Prop. 2.1]:

Proposition 5.2.

A class α∈Hd​(G,M)\alpha\in{\mathrm{H}}^{d}(G,M) is negligible if and only if ρZ∗​(α)=0\rho_{Z}^{*}(\alpha)=0, for some quasi-projective GG-variety ZZ over kk with generically free versal GG-action.

Proof.

The forward implication is trivial. For the reverse implication, given ρZ∗​(α)=0\rho_{Z}^{*}(\alpha)=0, there exists dense invariant open W⊂ZW\subset Z, such that the GG-action on WW is free, ρZ∗\rho_{Z}^{*} factors as

Hd​(G,M)→Hd​(W/G,M)→Hd​(𝔤k​(Z)G,M),{\mathrm{H}}^{d}(G,M)\to{\mathrm{H}}^{d}(W/G,M)\to{\mathrm{H}}^{d}(\mathfrak{g}_{k(Z)^{G}},M),

and α\alpha maps to 00 in the étale cohomology Hd​(W/G,M){\mathrm{H}}^{d}(W/G,M). Given a torsor T:L/KT\colon L/K, with corresponding ρK:𝔤K→G\rho_{K}\colon\mathfrak{g}_{K}\to G, there exists GG-equivariant Spec⁡(L)→W\mathrm{Spec}(L)\to W. Then ρK∗\rho_{K}^{*} also factors through Hd​(W/G,M){\mathrm{H}}^{d}(W/G,M), thus ρK∗​(α)=0\rho_{K}^{*}(\alpha)=0. ∎

Proposition 5.3.

Let XX be a smooth projective irreducible GG-variety with ℤ{\mathbb{Z}}-free finitely generated Pic⁡(X)\mathrm{Pic}(X), let ZZ be a quasi-projective GG-variety with generically free versal GG-action. Then the twisting construction by the associated torsor TZ=k⁡(Z)/k​(Z)GT_{Z}=k(Z)/k(Z)^{G} over K=k​(Z)GK=k(Z)^{G} gives rise to an isomorphism

Am2​(X,G)→∼Am2​(XTZ).\mathrm{Am}^{2}(X,G)\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\lower 1.5pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle\sim\,$}}}{{\to}}\mathrm{Am}^{2}({}^{T_{Z}}X).

Furthermore, the homomorphism

H2​(G,k×)→H2​(𝔤K,K¯×){\mathrm{H}}^{2}(G,k^{\times})\to{\mathrm{H}}^{2}(\mathfrak{g}_{K},\overline{K}^{\times})

is injective and restricts to the above isomorphism of Amitsur groups.

Proof.

The hypotheses imply H1​(X,𝒪X)=0{\mathrm{H}}^{1}(X,{\mathcal{O}}_{X})=0 and thus

Pic⁡(X×T)≅Pic⁡(X)⊕Pic⁡(T),\mathrm{Pic}(X\times T)\cong\mathrm{Pic}(X)\oplus\mathrm{Pic}(T),

for any finite-type kk-scheme TT. A standard limit arguments for coherent sheaves [Gro67, (8.5.2)] identifies Pic⁡(XTZ)\mathrm{Pic}({}^{T_{Z}}X) with

lim→⁡Pic⁡((X×W)/G),\varinjlim\mathrm{Pic}((X\times W)/G),

where the limit is over nonempty invariant affine open W⊂ZW\subset Z. A similar treatment of Pic⁡(Xk⁡(Z))\mathrm{Pic}(X_{k(Z)}), in combination with the expression for Picard group of a product with XX, gives an equivariant isomorphism

(5.2) Pic⁡(X)→∼Pic⁡(Xk⁡(Z)).\mathrm{Pic}(X)\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\lower 1.5pt\hbox{$\scriptstyle\sim\,$}}}{{\to}}\mathrm{Pic}(X_{k(Z)}).

Since group cohomology commutes with direct limits [Ser94, Prop. I.8], we may identify H2​(G,k​(Z)×){\mathrm{H}}^{2}(G,k(Z)^{\times}) with lim→⁡H2​(G,k​[W]×)\varinjlim{\mathrm{H}}^{2}(G,k[W]^{\times}). With this, we deduce that H2​(G,k×)→H2​(G,k​(Z)×){\mathrm{H}}^{2}(G,k^{\times})\to{\mathrm{H}}^{2}(G,k(Z)^{\times}) is injective by combining the vanishing of Am2​(Z,G)\mathrm{Am}^{2}(Z,G) (Proposition 5.1) with functoriality of the Leray spectral sequence and [AM20, Prop. 2.5 (iv)], which gives injectivity of Br⁡([Z/G]→Br⁡([W/G])CLOSE\mathrm{Br}([Z/G]\to\mathrm{Br}([W/G]). Now H2​(G,k​(Z)×){\mathrm{H}}^{2}(G,k(Z)^{\times}) is identified with the subgroup of Br⁡(K)≃H2​(𝔤K,K¯×)\mathrm{Br}(K)\simeq{\mathrm{H}}^{2}(\mathfrak{g}_{K},\overline{K}^{\times}), of classes, trivialized by restriction to k⁡(Z)k(Z); cf., e.g., [CTS21, Thm. 1.3.5].

We establish the isomorphism of Amitsur groups, first, in the case that Z=VZ=V, a linear representation with invariant open U⊂VU\subset V on which GG acts freely and complement of UU in VV of codimension ≥2\geq 2. Let nn denote the dimension of XX, and ℓ\ell the dimension of the representation VV. By [EG98, Thm. 1], we have

Pic⁡([X/G])≅CHn−1G​(X)≅CHn+ℓ−1​((X×U)/G).\mathrm{Pic}([X/G])\cong\mathrm{CH}^{G}_{n-1}(X)\cong\mathrm{CH}_{n+\ell-1}((X\times U)/G).

We have equivariant identifications of Pic⁡(X)≅CHn−1​(X)\mathrm{Pic}(X)\cong\mathrm{CH}_{n-1}(X), first, with CHn+ℓ−1​(X×V)\mathrm{CH}_{n+\ell-1}(X\times V), then with Pic⁡(X×U)≅CHn+ℓ−1​(X×U)\mathrm{Pic}(X\times U)\cong\mathrm{CH}_{n+\ell-1}(X\times U). In the commutative diagram

the bottom-left vertical map is surjective. So we have the isomorphism of Amitsur groups, compatible with the injective map on H2{\mathrm{H}}^{2}.

Now we treat the case of general ZZ. Basic functoriality gives the homomorphism of Amitsur groups, compatible with homomorphism on H2{\mathrm{H}}^{2}, and the latter is injective. By the isomorphism (5.2), the homomorphism of Amitsur groups is surjective. Now suppose we have a line bundle ℒ{\mathcal{L}} on XX with GG-invariant class in Pic⁡(X)\mathrm{Pic}(X), such that the class of ℒk⁡(Z){\mathcal{L}}_{k(Z)} on Xk⁡(Z)X_{k(Z)} lifts to Pic⁡(XTZ)\mathrm{Pic}({}^{T_{Z}}X), i.e., to Pic⁡((X×W)/G)\mathrm{Pic}((X\times W)/G) for some nonempty invariant affine open W⊂ZW\subset Z. By versality there exists an equivariant morphism Spec⁡(k⁡(V))→W\mathrm{Spec}(k(V))\to W. By a similar diagram as above, with Pic⁡((X×W)/G)\mathrm{Pic}((X\times W)/G) and Pic​(X×W)G\mathrm{Pic}(X\times W)^{G} in the middle row, and the established isomorphism Am2​(X,G)≅Am2​(XTV)\mathrm{Am}^{2}(X,G)\cong\mathrm{Am}^{2}({}^{T_{V}}X), we obtain the vanishing of the class of ℒ{\mathcal{L}} in Am2​(X,G)\mathrm{Am}^{2}(X,G). ∎

Example 5.4.

An analogous statement for higher Amitsur groups fails. There exist generically free regular actions of G=𝔔8G=\mathfrak{Q}_{8} on a del Pezzo surface XX of degree 2 with nontrivial Am3​(X,G)\mathrm{Am}^{3}(X,G) [TZ25]. If we take Z=VZ=V, faithful 22-dimensional representation, then k​(Z)Gk(Z)^{G} is a C2C_{2}-field, so Am3\mathrm{Am}^{3} has to vanish for the twist XTZ{}^{T_{Z}}X. Another example, with nontrivial Amn​(X,G)\mathrm{Am}^{n}(X,G) and vanishing Amn​(XTZ)\mathrm{Am}^{n}({}^{T_{Z}}X), for all n≥3n\geq 3, can be found in [STZ26, Sect. 9].

Instructions for reporting errors

We are continuing to improve HTML versions of papers, and your feedback helps enhance accessibility and mobile support. To report errors in the HTML that will help us improve conversion and rendering, choose any of the methods listed below:

  • Click the "Report Issue" () button, located in the page header.

Tip: You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.

Our team has already identified the following issues. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for all.

Have a free development cycle? Help support accessibility at arXiv! Our collaborators at LaTeXML maintain a list of packages that need conversion, and welcome developer contributions.
